mission: Progressive session-analysis scheduling: events closing while recording continues (E1 closes -> analyze while E2 records). Stress: rapid rallies, backlog, failed extraction, abstained events, interruption/recovery. Measure queue latency and correctness under load.

configuration.scheduler: session-scheduler-1 (bounded-concurrency FIFO over SessionEventEngine closures · retryable-failure revert-to-pending · suspend/resume + recoverPending)
configuration.engine: real SessionEventEngine (D-029 adaptive completion, append-only frontier) — NOT mocked
configuration.simulatedSeam: only the SessionAnalysisExecutor (analysis execution) is modeled; native clip extraction is unavailable on Linux
configuration.prng: deterministic seeded PRNG; latencies are stream-time ms, not device time

datasetScope: Fully synthetic wrist-speed streams (Gaussian bumps) driving the real engine; no gold labels, no held-out cases (wm-dink-01, afn-vic-rally1 untouched), no device numbers claimed.

rapid-rally-backlog.note: 1 slot with 3-4s service on 1.3s stroke cadence saturates as expected; FIFO order preserved, no loss

rapid-rally-2slots.note: 2 slots eliminate the backlog on the same rapid rally (p95 wait 41400 -> 1360 ms)

flaky-extraction.note: failed extraction reverts events to pending (never fabricated ready/abstain); exhausted retries stay pending with retry_exhausted

interruption-recovery.note: suspend() during 12-18s window queues closures without dispatch; resume() drains; recoverPending({readmitExhausted:true}) after simulated restart completes all 18

correctness.checks: per-scenario engine-state vs scheduler-terminal agreement, FIFO order, no duplicate dispatch, no event loss, ready-requires-analysis, terminal-states-immutable

gates.pnpm test: pass (all packages; analysis-pipeline 47/47 incl. 10 new scheduler tests)

honesty: Stream is synthetic; scheduler and session engine are the real production implementations. Only the executor seam is modeled. No Mac/iPhone/device latency claimed; all latencies are scheduling latencies in stream-time ms.
